def: The fast on-package memory of a data-centre GPU, whose fixed capacity (for example 80 GB) limits what can be trained on one device.
The weights, gradients and optimiser state of a model, whose total size scales with the number of parameters and not with the batch.
The extra values an optimiser stores per weight, such as Adam's two moment estimates and the full-precision master copy of the weights.
A 32-bit copy of the weights that receives the updates in mixed-precision training, because bf16 cannot represent small updates.
The intermediate outputs of each layer saved during the forward pass so the backward pass can compute gradients; their size grows with batch and sequence length.
A 16-bit floating-point format with the exponent range of 32-bit floats but only about 8 significant bits, widely used for training.
Summing gradients over several micro-batches before one optimiser step, giving the gradient of a large batch while holding only a small batch's activations.
Saving only some layers' inputs and recomputing the rest during the backward pass, trading about one extra forward pass for much less activation memory.
Recomputing only the memory-heavy but cheap parts of a layer, such as attention scores, instead of the whole layer.
The error raised when the memory a training step requests at its peak exceeds the GPU's capacity.
A framework component that keeps freed GPU memory blocks for reuse, so tools report more memory reserved than tensors actually use.
